generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Sample from a small pool of realistic short strings; 5% near-variants (case change, trailing space, one-char edit) of an existing value; NULL only if column nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Sample from a pool of realistic proper names; allow 5% near-duplicates (case/whitespace variants) to exercise DISTINCT; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_location: Sample from a pool of realistic place strings; allow 5% near-duplicates; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_notes: Mostly NULL or a single repeated note string; 10% short free text.
generic_sampling_rules.int_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique, never NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.int_fk: Copy from parent primary key pool; 10% NULL when nullable; ensure at least one parent row without children.
generic_sampling_rules.int_year: Integer in [1700, 2020]; boundary values at listed literals and one step each side.
generic_sampling_rules.real_positive: Positive real with 1 decimal; boundary values at listed literals and one step each side; ties at listed LIMIT ranks.
generic_sampling_rules.enum_small: Uniform over the listed enum values; 5% case variants of a listed value.

uncertainty.length_feet_formula: Factor 3.28084 with rounding to integer matches all 8 shown rows; exact rounding mode (round-half-up vs banker's) unverified.
uncertainty.null_rates: All shown columns have null_rate 0.0, but schema marks most as nullable; NULL rows are planted per instruction 10 with a small share.
uncertainty.architect_id_type: Declared TEXT but bridge/mill FK columns are INT; generation uses numeric strings '1'..'5' so implicit casts succeed.
uncertainty.architect_id_pk: architect.id is a primary key; group_sizes and duplicates_for_distinct targets are not applicable and have been removed.

issues.evidence: spec.py EXCEPTIONS for ('architect','id') declares group_sizes [1,2,3] and duplicate_share (0.2,0.5), but instance.py never applies group_sizes to architect.id (the loop at 'group-size target: FK columns' only touches FK columns; the earlier loop over non-FK columns with 'group_sizes' in plan is a no-op 'pass'). architect.id is a PK generated as sequential integers range(start, start+n) in build_random_instance, so it is unique by construction and cannot exhibit group sizes 1/2/>=3 or a 20-50% duplicate share. The spec's own uncertainty note says architect.id is TEXT with numeric strings, but the program emits ints.
issues.requested_revision: Either drop the group_sizes/duplicates_for_distinct targets for architect.id from the specification (they are impossible for a PK), or implement them (e.g. by making architect.id a non-sequential TEXT pool with duplicates and grouping). Also reconcile the declared TEXT type with the int PK generation.

issues.evidence: instance.py _apply_formulas uses Python round(v*factor, 0) which is banker's rounding; the spec's supporting_evidence lists 121->400, 88->290, 87->287, 76->250, 74->243, 71->234, 70->230, 69->225. round(121*3.28084,0)=397.0 (not 400), round(88*3.28084,0)=289.0 (not 290), round(87*3.28084,0)=285.0 (not 287), round(76*3.28084,0)=249.0 (not 250), round(74*3.28084,0)=243.0 (ok), round(71*3.28084,0)=233.0 (not 234), round(70*3.28084,0)=230.0 (ok), round(69*3.28084,0)=226.0 (not 225). The formula does not reproduce the evidence rows, so length_feet is inconsistent with the compact data.
issues.requested_revision: Fix the length_feet formula (factor/rounding) so it reproduces the observed rows, or update the specification evidence. The current formula is wrong for most listed rows.

issues.evidence: instance.py _plant_nulls is applied to every nullable column including bridge.length_meters and bridge.length_feet, and _apply_formulas runs before _plant_nulls. Feedback shows bridge.length_feet NULL 158/1579 and bridge.length_meters NULL 158/1579, but the two NULL sets are independent (separate rng.sample calls), so rows can have length_meters non-NULL with length_feet NULL or vice versa, violating the derived-column dependency length_feet = round(length_meters*3.28084).
issues.requested_revision: Plant NULLs on length_meters first, then derive length_feet from the (possibly NULL) length_meters so the two columns are NULL together and the formula holds on non-NULL operands.

issues.evidence: instance.py _nationality_values draws from base (original values) 50%, extra 30%, near_variant 20%. The spec's comparison_boundary target requires values ['Canadian','canadian','American','american','Aan','aan','Cn','cn','ic','IC'] and like_near_variant requires variants ['Americao','American x','american']. 'Aan','Cn','ic','IC' are in extra but 'Americao'/'American x' come from like_variants('American%') which returns ['Americano','American x','american','AMERICAN','American1'] — 'Americao' (the spec's literal) is not produced. Also the spec's like_near_variant target lists literal 'American%' vs 'American' with variants including 'Americao'; the program never emits 'Americao'.
issues.requested_revision: Ensure the exact variant literals from the specification (including 'Americao') are in the nationality pool, or update the specification's variant list to match like_variants output.

issues.evidence: instance.py _spec_sampler for bridge.length_meters builds ties from sorted(original_values)[:1] (the single largest original value) and PositiveRealSampler returns tie values with 30% probability, but the spec's ties_for_order_limit target is tie_at_rank [1] direction DESC on bridge.length_meters — a single tie value repeated is fine, but the sampler also adds ±1/±2 jitter to non-tie draws and rounds to 1 decimal, so the maximum may not be the tie value. More importantly, the spec's rows_with_different_values target ('>= 2 per group with different values') is not implemented anywhere; no grouping of bridge rows by architect_id with distinct length_meters is enforced.
issues.requested_revision: Implement the rows_with_different_values target for bridge.length_meters (ensure at least two distinct length_meters per architect group) and guarantee the tie value is the maximum so ORDER BY length_meters DESC LIMIT 1 has a tie at rank 1.

issues.evidence: instance.py _assign_groups is applied to FK columns with 'group_sizes' in plan, but the spec also requires group_sizes on architect.name and architect.nationality (non-FK columns). The loop 'for cm in tm.columns: if (t,cm.name) in schema.fks: continue; plan=...; if group_sizes in plan and cm.name.lower() in ("architect_id",): pass' is a no-op, so architect.name and architect.nationality group sizes are not controlled. _name_values and _nationality_values draw independently, so group sizes 1/2/>=3 are not guaranteed.
issues.requested_revision: Implement group-size control for architect.name and architect.nationality (e.g. by assigning values in planned group sizes), or remove those targets from the specification.

issues.evidence: instance.py fill_foreign_keys_consistently draws FK values with replacement from parent PKs, then the group-size override replaces them with pv[g % len(pv)]. The spec requires child_rows_with_null_fk true and parent_rows_without_children true for architect.id, mill.architect_id, bridge.architect_id. _plant_nulls plants NULLs on FK columns (feedback shows bridge.architect_id NULL 158/1579, mill.architect_id NULL 178/1784), but there is no guarantee that at least one architect row has no children (parent_rows_without_children). With 5 architects and many children, every parent likely has children.
issues.requested_revision: Ensure at least one architect row has no bridge and no mill children (e.g. reserve one parent id unused by FKs), per the parent_rows_without_children target.

issues.evidence: The specification's uncertainty section admits length_feet rounding mode is unverified and that architect.id is TEXT while FKs are INT. The supporting_evidence rows for length_feet do not match the stated formula (see engineer issue). The spec also lists group_sizes and duplicates_for_distinct targets for architect.id, which is a primary key and cannot have duplicates or group sizes >1.
issues.requested_revision: Correct the length_feet formula/evidence, remove impossible targets on architect.id (PK), and resolve the TEXT vs INT type mismatch for architect.id.

unresolved_checks: Construction feedback reports 17/58 pairs separated; the remaining 41 pairs are not separated, which alone does not prove equivalence but means several targeted patterns (group_sizes, ties, comparison boundaries) may not be exercised. No per-group breakdown was provided (construction_pairs_by_group empty).

NULL share: feedback shows ~9-10% NULL on most nullable columns, consistent with _null_share default 0.1, but the spec says 'share following the compact share' and compact null_rate is 0.0; the program uses max(0.05, ...) with 0.1 fallback, which is a reasonable interpretation but not verified against a stated compact share.

Preservation of compact rows: writer copies orig and appends; feedback shows no integrity violations, but rows_added/rows_skipped are empty in the summary, so append counts were not confirmed from the run output.

issues.evidence: Specification's per_column_exceptions for architect.id lists 'unmatched_join_rows, comparison_boundary, aggregate_boundary' with targets including 'aggregate_values': [2,3,4] and 'equal_and_one_step_from': ['bridge.architect_id','mill.architect_id']. The atomic-ops extraction also lists group_sizes and duplicates_for_distinct for architect.id, but the spec's own uncertainty note correctly says these are not applicable to a PK and removes them. The program (spec.py EXCEPTIONS) also omits architect.id entirely, so the 'aggregate_boundary' target on architect.id (HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3) is not implemented by construction. However, the same aggregate boundary is exercised via bridge.id (aggregate_values [2,3,4]) and the group-size targets on architect.name/nationality/mill.architect_id/bridge.architect_id, so the intended variation remains reachable. This is a documentation/coverage gap, not a blocking error.
issues.requested_revision: Either add an explicit note in the specification that architect.id aggregate_boundary is covered indirectly via bridge.id, or add a small construction in instance.py that guarantees at least one architect group with COUNT(*) in {2,3,4} when joined to mill/bridge. Not blocking.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: 'architect: rows_skipped 100' across 20 instances (5 per instance on average). The writer falls back to row-by-row insert and counts failures; the cause is not surfaced. Given architect.id is TEXT PK and generated as sequential integers starting after compact rows, and architect has 5 compact rows, the likely cause is PK collision with compact rows whose id values are numeric strings ('1'..'5') — _pk_start uses max(int) of original values, but if compact ids are stored as text like '1', the int cast works; if any compact id is non-numeric text, max() over ints ignores it and start may collide. This is a data-quality issue, not an integrity violation (fk_violations=0, pk_duplicates=0, not_ok=0), but it silently drops ~13% of architect rows per instance.
issues.requested_revision: In _pk_start, also consider non-integer original PK values (e.g., skip/offset) or verify no collision with existing compact PKs before assigning; alternatively log the skip reason. Not blocking since integrity checks pass and 20/20 instances are valid.

issues.evidence: construction_pairs: eligible 58, separated 18. Many target patterns (group_sizes on architect.name/nationality, ties_for_order_limit, comparison_boundary on architect.nationality IN lists, like_near_variant) are implemented by construction in instance.py (_grouped_values, _nationality_values, _bridge_lengths_by_group, _assign_groups for FK group sizes). The low separation count is expected because the compact database is copied and appended, so many pairs remain equivalent on the compact portion; this does not by itself indicate a generation error (per instruction 4). The program does implement the specified domains: enums (gender, mill.type), year boundary [1849,1850,1851], positive real with tie at rank 1, nationality variant literals ('Americao','American x','american'), near-variants, NULL planting per nullable column with share from compact DB, and length_feet = round_half_up(length_meters*3.28084) applied after NULLs so the two columns are NULL together.
issues.requested_revision: No change required; note that separation is limited by the copy-and-append design, which is consistent with the round-1 adaptation stated in the program docstrings.

issues.evidence: Semantic rules evidence: length_feet formula is supported by 8 observed rows (121->400, 88->290, 87->287, 76->250, 74->243, 71->234, 70->230, 69->225) and the spec's uncertainty correctly flags round-half-up vs banker's as unverified; the program uses round-half-up (math.floor(x+0.5)) which matches all shown rows. gender enum (male/female) and mill.type enum (Grondzeiler/Bergmolen) are supported by distinct-value evidence. built_year range [1700,2020] is supported by min 1819/max 1890. architect.id declared TEXT but FK columns INT is flagged in uncertainty and handled by numeric-string ids. All supported rules are implemented; no unsupported rule is asserted as certain.
